newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli unlinked and short-term bonds up.
newsitem.headline: Israeli unlinked and short-term bonds up.

text.p: Israeli unlinked and short-term bonds closed up on Monday while those linked to the dollar and inflation were down as the market waited for the Bank of Israel announcement on its key interest rate, traders said.
After the market closed, the central bank said it would hold the lending rate unchanged for December at an annualised 15.2 percent.
* Unlinked government bonds (Gilon - issued for four years): +0.07 pct to 170.5.
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: +0.01 pct to 160.95
Volume was moderate at 148 million shekels with unlinked bonds rising on expectations for a minimal rate cut.

"CPI-linked bonds fell today with medium-term bonds posting the sharpest decline. The main reason for the decline was that the Bank of Israel issued a new series of linked bonds," said Baruch Glicksberg at Clal Insurance.

"Yields on the inflation-linked bonds fell sharply during the last few months to 4.5 percent. At the current level the market reached a saturation point," said another trader. "Unlinked bonds rose mildly as the market expected a moderate rate cut of 0.2 to 0.3 percentage points."

"The Makams rose mildly in very dull and mixed trading as investors predicted a minimal rate cut. Investors realized today that the central bank will not lower the rate by 0.5 percentage point. Yields on the (one year) Makam remained unchanged at 14.8 percent, which is relatively low," Glicksberg said.
Traders said that dollar linked bonds closed slightly lower after the shekel remained stable against the dollar.
The representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.2470 shekels, unchanged from Friday.
Note: Makams are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year. The Bank of Israel issues Makams to absorb liquidity.
